en: Mount Mayon in Albay is famous for its perfect cone shape and is the most active volcano in the Philippines.
The Philippine eagle is the national bird and is endemic to the heavy forests of the island of Mindanao.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through the Cagayan Valley before emptying into the sea.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features a navigable underground river that flows directly into the West Philippine Sea.
Lake Taal in Batangas is a complex volcano with a main crater lake that contains Volcano Island, which itself has a crater lake.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site known for its pristine coral atolls.
Boracay is a small island in the province of Aklan famous for its White Beach, which consists of fine white coral sand.
Baguio City in the Cordillera Administrative Region is known as the Summer Capital of the Philippines due to its cool climate.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of at least 1,268 symmetrical mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
The Tamaraw is a critically endangered dwarf buffalo species found exclusively in the grasslands and forests of Mindoro island.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao province were carved into the mountains by indigenous people over 2,000 years ago.
